items.title: 5.3 Equations of Medians, Altitudes and Right Bisectors

source_refs.note: Book p. 146-148: 5.3 Examples 7 (medians), 8 (altitudes), 9 (right bisectors) with Figures 5.2-5.4 and four Remember! boxes

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
This section uses only two tools from 5.1: the mid-point formula and the point-slope form \(y - y_{1} = m(x - x_{1})\). Every line here passes through a known point; only the slope must be found.
Median: through a vertex and the mid-point of the opposite side (two points known).
Altitude: through a vertex, perpendicular to the opposite side (slope \(= -\frac{1}{\text{slope of side}}\)).
Right bisector: through the mid-point of a side, perpendicular to that side.

rows: a vertex and the mid-point of the opposite side
blocks.caption: Our summary: median, altitude, right bisector

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: A median joins the vertex of a triangle to the mid-point of the opposite side.

blocks.title: Example 7
blocks.problem: Triangle \(ABC\) has vertices \(A(2, 3)\), \(B(4, 5)\) and \(C(-2, 7)\). Find the equations of medians of the triangle \(ABC\).
steps:
Given: \(A(2, 3)\), \(B(4, 5)\) and \(C(-2, 7)\).
To find: the equations of the three medians.
Method: find the mid-points of the sides; each median then passes through two known points (a vertex and a mid-point), so we use the two-point form.

Mid-points of the sides
Let \(D\), \(E\) and \(F\) be the mid-points of the sides \(BC\), \(AC\) and \(AB\) respectively.
\[D\left(\dfrac{4 + (-2)}{2}, \dfrac{5 + 7}{2}\right) = D(1, 6)\]
\[E\left(\dfrac{2 + (-2)}{2}, \dfrac{3 + 7}{2}\right) = E(0, 5)\]
\[F\left(\dfrac{2 + 4}{2}, \dfrac{3 + 5}{2}\right) = F(3, 4)\]
Why: the median from \(A\) goes to the mid-point of the opposite side \(BC\), and so on.

Median AD
Equation of the median \(AD\) is
\[\dfrac{y - 3}{3 - 6} = \dfrac{x - 2}{2 - 1}\]
\[y - 3 = -3(x - 2)\]
\[3x + y - 9 = 0\]
Why: two-point form with \(A(2, 3)\) and \(D(1, 6)\): \(\frac{y - y_{1}}{y_{1} - y_{2}} = \frac{x - x_{1}}{x_{1} - x_{2}}\). Then \(y - 3 = -3x + 6\).

Median BE
Equation of the median \(BE\) is
\[\dfrac{y - 5}{5 - 5} = \dfrac{x - 4}{4 - 0}\]
\[y - 5 = 0\]
Why: \(B(4, 5)\) and \(E(0, 5)\) have the same y-coordinate, so the slope is \(\frac{5 - 5}{4 - 0} = 0\): a horizontal line. (The printed fraction has denominator 0; it is shorthand for \(y - 5 = 0 \cdot (x - 4)\).)

Median CF
Equation of the median \(CF\) is
\[\dfrac{y - 7}{7 - 4} = \dfrac{x + 2}{-2 - 3}\]
\[-5(y - 7) = 3(x + 2)\]
\[3x + 5y - 29 = 0\]
Why: two-point form with \(C(-2, 7)\) and \(F(3, 4)\); cross-multiplying gives \(-5y + 35 = 3x + 6\).

Check:
\(D(1, 6)\): \(3 + 6 - 9 = 0\). \(F(3, 4)\): \(9 + 20 - 29 = 0\). The three medians meet at the centroid
\[G\left(\dfrac{2 + 4 - 2}{3}, \dfrac{3 + 5 + 7}{3}\right) = G\left(\dfrac{4}{3}, 5\right)\]
and indeed \(3 \cdot \frac{4}{3} + 5 - 9 = 0\), \(y = 5\), \(3 \cdot \frac{4}{3} + 25 - 29 = 0\).

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: An altitude is the line drawn from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: If \(m_{1}\) and \(m_{2}\) be the slopes of perpendicular lines then \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Why \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\)? Turning a line through \(90^\circ\) turns its direction \((1, m)\) into \((-m, 1)\), whose slope is \(-\frac{1}{m}\). So the slope of a perpendicular is the negative reciprocal: flip the fraction and change the sign. For example, slope \(\frac{3}{7}\) gives \(-\frac{7}{3}\). (This works when neither line is vertical or horizontal.)

blocks.title: Example 8
blocks.problem: \(A(1, 2)\), \(B(5, -1)\) and \(C(-2, -4)\) are the vertices of \(\triangle ABC\). Find the equations of altitudes of triangle \(ABC\).
steps:
Given: \(A(1, 2)\), \(B(5, -1)\), \(C(-2, -4)\).
To find: the equations of the three altitudes.
Method: an altitude passes through a vertex and is perpendicular to the opposite side. So for each one: slope of the side, then the perpendicular slope \(-\frac{1}{m}\), then point-slope form through the vertex.
Let \(\overline{AE}\), \(\overline{BF}\) and \(\overline{CD}\) be the altitudes of the sides \(BC\), \(CA\) and \(AB\) of the triangle respectively.

Altitude AE: slopes
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{BC} = \dfrac{-4 - (-1)}{-2 - 5} = \dfrac{3}{7}\]
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{AE} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{BC}} = -\dfrac{7}{3}\]
Why: \(AE \perp BC\), so the product of their slopes is \(-1\).

Altitude AE: equation
Equation of the altitude \(AE\) is
\[y - 2 = -\dfrac{7}{3}(x - 1)\]
\[3y - 6 = -7x + 7\]
\[7x + 3y - 13 = 0\]
Why: point-slope form through the vertex \(A(1, 2)\); multiply by 3 to clear the fraction.

Altitude BF: slopes
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{CA} = \dfrac{2 - (-4)}{1 - (-2)} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2\]
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{BF} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{CA}} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
Why: \(BF \perp CA\).

Altitude BF: equation
Equation of the altitude \(BF\) is
\[y + 1 = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 5)\]
\[x + 2y - 3 = 0\]
Why: point-slope form through \(B(5, -1)\); then \(2y + 2 = -x + 5\).

Altitude CD: slopes
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{AB} = \dfrac{-1 - 2}{5 - 1} = -\dfrac{3}{4}\]
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{CD} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{AB}} = \dfrac{4}{3}\]
Why: \(CD \perp AB\); the negative reciprocal of \(-\frac{3}{4}\) is \(+\frac{4}{3}\).

Altitude CD: equation
Equation of the altitude \(CD\) is
\[y + 4 = \dfrac{4}{3}(x + 2)\]
\[4x - 3y - 4 = 0\]
Why: point-slope form through \(C(-2, -4)\); then \(3y + 12 = 4x + 8\).

Check:
Each vertex lies on its altitude: \(A\): \(7 + 6 - 13 = 0\); \(B\): \(5 - 2 - 3 = 0\); \(C\): \(-8 + 12 - 4 = 0\). Solving \(AE\) and \(BF\) gives \((\frac{17}{11}, \frac{8}{11})\), and \(4 \cdot \frac{17}{11} - 3 \cdot \frac{8}{11} - 4 = \frac{68 - 24 - 44}{11} = 0\): the three altitudes meet at one point (the orthocentre).

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: A perpendicular or right bisector of a triangle is a line that is perpendicular to one side of the triangle and passes through the mid point of that side.

blocks.title: Example 9
blocks.problem: Triangle \(ABC\) has vertices \(A(-3, 2)\), \(B(5, 4)\) and \(C(3, -8)\). Find the equations of right bisectors of triangle \(ABC\).
steps:
Given: \(A(-3, 2)\), \(B(5, 4)\), \(C(3, -8)\).
To find: the equations of the three right bisectors.
Method: a right bisector passes through the mid-point of a side and is perpendicular to it. For each side: mid-point, slope of the side, negative reciprocal, point-slope form.

Mid-points of the sides
Let \(D\), \(E\) and \(F\) be the mid-points of the sides \(BC\), \(CA\) and \(AB\) respectively.
\[D\left(\dfrac{5 + 3}{2}, \dfrac{4 + (-8)}{2}\right) = D(4, -2)\]
\[E\left(\dfrac{-3 + 3}{2}, \dfrac{2 + (-8)}{2}\right) = E(0, -3)\]
\[F\left(\dfrac{-3 + 5}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 4}{2}\right) = F(1, 3)\]
Why: each right bisector must pass through one of these points.

Right bisector of AB
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{AB} = \dfrac{4 - 2}{5 - (-3)} = \dfrac{2}{8} = \dfrac{1}{4}\]
\[\text{Slope of right bisector to } \overline{AB} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{AB}} = -4\]
Equation of the right bisector to \(\overline{AB}\) is:
\[y - 3 = -4(x - 1)\]
\[4x + y - 7 = 0\]
Why: point-slope form through the mid-point \(F(1, 3)\) with the perpendicular slope.

Right bisector of BC
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{BC} = \dfrac{-8 - 4}{3 - 5} = \dfrac{-12}{-2} = 6\]
\[\text{Slope of right bisector to } \overline{BC} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{BC}} = -\dfrac{1}{6}\]
Equation of the right bisector to \(\overline{BC}\) is:
\[y + 2 = -\dfrac{1}{6}(x - 4)\]
\[x + 6y + 8 = 0\]
Why: through \(D(4, -2)\); multiply by 6: \(6y + 12 = -x + 4\).

Right bisector of CA
\[\text{Slope of } \overline{CA} = \dfrac{2 - (-8)}{-3 - 3} = \dfrac{10}{-6} = -\dfrac{5}{3}\]
\[\text{Slope of right bisector to } \overline{CA} = \dfrac{-1}{\text{Slope of } \overline{CA}} = \dfrac{3}{5}\]
Equation of the right bisector to \(\overline{CA}\) is
\[y + 3 = \dfrac{3}{5}(x - 0)\]
\[3x - 5y - 15 = 0\]
Why: through \(E(0, -3)\); multiply by 5: \(5y + 15 = 3x\).

Check:
Solving the first two bisectors gives \(O(\frac{50}{23}, -\frac{39}{23})\); then \(3 \cdot \frac{50}{23} - 5\left(-\frac{39}{23}\right) - 15 = \frac{150 + 195 - 345}{23} = 0\), so all three meet at \(O\). Also \(OA^{2} = OB^{2} = OC^{2} = \frac{21386}{529}\): \(O\) is equidistant from the vertices (the circumcentre), as every point of a right bisector is equidistant from the ends of its side.
blocks.answer: Right bisector of \(\overline{AB}\): \(4x + y - 7 = 0\); of \(\overline{BC}\): \(x + 6y + 8 = 0\); of \(\overline{CA}\): \(3x - 5y - 15 = 0\).

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Median: vertex + mid-point of the opposite side; two-point form.
2. Altitude: through a vertex, slope \(= -\frac{1}{\text{slope of opposite side}}\).
3. Right bisector: through the mid-point of a side, slope \(= -\frac{1}{\text{slope of that side}}\).
4. Perpendicular lines: \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\).
5. Check: the three medians (altitudes, right bisectors) of a triangle always meet at one point; use that point to test your three equations.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Taking the altitude through the mid-point, or the right bisector through the vertex. Altitude: vertex. Right bisector: mid-point.
2. Forgetting to change the sign in the negative reciprocal: perpendicular to slope 6 is \(-\frac{1}{6}\), not \(\frac{1}{6}\).
3. Pairing a vertex with the wrong mid-point: the median from \(A\) goes to the mid-point of \(BC\), not of \(AB\).
4. Sign slips with negative coordinates in the slope formula, e.g. \(2 - (-8) = 10\).
